note: Original questions written for this app. They follow the IFAB Laws of the Game; questions tagged 'hs' cover where NFHS high school rules differ.

questions.q: The ball is sitting exactly on top of the touchline. Is it in or out?
choices: In — the line is part of the field
Only in if a player is also on the line
questions.why: Lines belong to the area they bound. The ball is out only once the whole ball has crossed the whole line.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT marked on a full field?
choices: A second penalty spot at the halfway line
questions.why: There is one penalty mark per penalty area. The halfway line has a centre mark, not a penalty spot.

questions.q: A goal is scored but the corner flag had fallen over earlier. What now?
choices: The goal stands; a missing flag does not void play
No goal, restart with a dropped ball
questions.why: A fallen flag is fixed at the next stoppage. It does not invalidate play.

questions.q: The ball goes soft in the middle of play. What does the referee do?
choices: Stop play and restart with a dropped ball
Let play finish and swap it at half-time
Award a free kick to whoever asked
questions.why: A defective ball means play stops and restarts with a dropped ball where it became defective.

questions.q: Which ball size do most U8 leagues use?
questions.why: Size 3 is typical up to about U8, size 4 through roughly U12, size 5 from U13. Check your league.

questions.q: The ball bursts as it crosses the goal line for a goal. What is the decision?
choices: No goal if it was already defective before crossing
Goal, because it crossed the line
questions.why: If the ball was defective before it crossed, no goal. Restart with a dropped ball.

questions.q: When may a substitute enter the field?
choices: Only with the referee's permission, after the outgoing player leaves
As soon as the ball goes out
Any time, as long as they enter at the halfway line
questions.why: The referee must be informed, play stopped, and the outgoing player off before the substitute enters.

questions.q: How few players can a team have before a match cannot continue?
questions.why: A match may not start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.

questions.q: Under NFHS high school rules, substitutions are:
choices: Much freer than the Laws, allowed at many stoppages
questions.why: NFHS allows free substitution at many stoppages, with rules on which team may substitute and when.

questions.q: A player arrives wearing a thin bracelet they cannot get off. What happens?
choices: They cannot play until it is removed
They may play if it is taped over
They may play if the referee did not see it
questions.why: All jewellery is forbidden and must be removed. Taping over it is not permitted.

questions.q: Shin guards must be:
choices: Worn outside the socks so they can be seen
questions.why: Shin guards are compulsory and must be covered entirely by the socks.

questions.q: A goalkeeper's shirt is the same colour as the opponents' shirts. What must happen?
choices: The keeper must change to a distinguishing colour
Play on; only outfield shirts matter
questions.why: Goalkeepers must wear colours distinguishing them from the other players and the match officials.

questions.q: You disagree strongly with a decision. What is the correct response?
choices: Ask the referee to explain it right away
questions.why: Decisions on facts connected with play are final. Dissent can be cautioned.

questions.q: The referee awards a goal, then the assistant flags for offside before the restart. Can it change?
choices: Yes, because play has not restarted
questions.why: A referee may change a decision on realising it is wrong, provided play has not restarted.

questions.q: Under NFHS rules, the officiating crew often uses:
choices: Always one referee and two assistants
questions.why: Many states use dual or double-dual systems rather than the single-referee diagonal.

questions.q: An assistant referee flags for offside but the referee waves play on. What stands?
choices: The flag, because the assistant is closer
Play stops for a dropped ball
questions.why: Assistants advise. The referee holds final authority.

questions.q: Which is NOT a duty of the assistant referee?
choices: Signalling the ball out of play
questions.why: Only the referee issues cards. Assistants indicate but do not sanction.

questions.q: Why does the referee play past the scheduled time?
choices: To make up for time lost to stoppages
To let the losing team equalise
questions.why: Allowance is made for substitutions, injuries, time-wasting, sanctions and celebrations.

questions.q: Time expires while a penalty kick is about to be taken. What happens?
choices: The half is extended so the penalty can be completed
It carries over to the second half
questions.why: The half is extended to allow a penalty kick to be taken and completed.

questions.q: A varsity NFHS match is normally:
choices: Two 40-minute halves on a clock that stops
questions.why: NFHS varsity is two 40-minute halves with a stopping clock, not a running clock with added time.

questions.q: Can a goal be scored directly from kick-off?
choices: No, it must touch another player
questions.why: A goal may be scored directly from kick-off against the opponents.

questions.q: At kick-off, which way must the ball be played?
questions.why: Since 2019 the ball may be played in any direction at kick-off.

questions.q: How is a modern dropped ball taken?
choices: Dropped for one player, everyone else 4.5m away
questions.why: Dropped balls are no longer contested. It goes to one player, or the keeper if in their own penalty area.

questions.q: When is the ball out of play?
choices: Only when the whole ball crosses the whole line
As soon as it touches the line
When the referee loses sight of it
questions.why: The whole ball must wholly cross the line, on the ground or in the air.

questions.q: The ball rebounds off the corner flag and stays on the field. What now?
choices: Play on, it is still in play
questions.why: Rebounds off the flag, posts, bar or an official on the field leave the ball in play.

questions.q: The ball strikes the referee and a goal is scored directly as a result. The restart is:
questions.why: If contact with an official leads directly to a goal, a promising attack or a change of possession, play restarts with a dropped ball.

questions.q: What makes a goal?
choices: The whole ball crosses the whole goal line between the posts and under the bar
Any part of the ball crosses the line
questions.why: The whole of the ball must pass over the line between the posts and beneath the crossbar.

questions.q: The goalkeeper throws the ball directly into the opponents' goal. Decision?
choices: No goal — goal kick to the opponents
questions.why: A goal cannot be scored directly from a goalkeeper's throw. A goal kick is awarded.

questions.q: Is standing in an offside position an offence?
choices: No, not until you get involved in play
questions.why: Position alone is not punished. It becomes an offence only on involvement.

questions.q: From which restart can a player NOT be penalised for offside?
questions.why: There is no offside offence directly from a throw-in, goal kick or corner kick.

questions.q: A player in an offside position runs onto a rebound off the goalkeeper. Decision?
choices: Play on, the keeper touched it
questions.why: Gaining an advantage from a rebound or deflection counts as involvement.

questions.q: Which body parts count when judging offside position?
choices: Head, body and feet — not the arms
questions.why: Arms and hands are excluded, because you cannot score with them.

questions.q: The restart for an offside offence is:
choices: An indirect free kick where the offence occurred
questions.why: Offside is punished with an indirect free kick from the position of the offence.

questions.q: The ball hits a defender's arm which is tucked against their side. Handball?
choices: Always, any arm contact is handball
Only if it goes in the goal
questions.why: A natural position that does not make the body unnaturally bigger is generally not an offence.

questions.q: Which offence brings an INDIRECT free kick?
choices: Playing in a dangerous manner with no contact
questions.why: Dangerous play without contact and impeding without contact are indirect. Contact fouls are direct.

questions.q: 'Reckless' means the player:
choices: Acted with disregard for danger — caution
questions.why: Careless means no card, reckless means a caution, excessive force means a sending off.

questions.q: A defender handles the ball to deny an obvious goal-scoring opportunity in their own area. Decision?
choices: Penalty kick and a sending off
questions.why: Denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by handling is a sending-off offence.

questions.q: Under NFHS rules, a player shown a yellow card:
choices: Must leave the field and may be substituted
questions.why: This is one of the biggest NFHS departures. A cautioned player leaves and may be replaced.

questions.q: How do you know a free kick is indirect?
choices: The referee holds an arm up until it is taken
The kick is taken from the touchline
questions.why: The raised arm stays up until the ball touches another player or leaves play.

questions.q: An indirect free kick is struck straight into the goal without anyone touching it. Decision?
choices: No goal — goal kick to the defending team
questions.why: An indirect free kick must touch another player before it can count as a goal.

questions.q: At a free kick, how far must opponents retreat in the full-sized game?
questions.why: 9.15m, though small-sided leagues scale it down, commonly to 5 or 6 metres.

questions.q: Where must the goalkeeper be when a penalty is struck?
choices: On or in line with the goal line, part of one foot touching
questions.why: At least part of one foot must be on, above or behind the goal line when the ball is kicked.

questions.q: Feinting in the run-up to a penalty is:
questions.why: Feinting during the run-up is allowed. Feinting after completing the run-up is not.

questions.q: Which makes a throw-in legal?
choices: Both feet down, both hands, from behind and over the head
One foot may lift if you are quick
Either hand, as long as it is overhead
questions.why: Part of each foot on the line or ground outside it, both hands, delivered from behind and over the head.

questions.q: A throw-in goes straight into the opponents' goal without touching anyone. Decision?
questions.why: A goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in.

questions.q: A throw-in goes straight into the thrower's OWN goal. Decision?
questions.why: No goal can be scored directly from a throw-in, so a corner is awarded to the opponents.

questions.q: On a goal kick, when is the ball in play?
choices: As soon as it is kicked and clearly moves
Once it leaves the penalty area
Once an outfield player touches it
questions.why: Since 2019 the ball no longer has to leave the penalty area.

questions.q: An attacker is standing inside the penalty area when the goal kick is taken. Decision?
choices: Indirect free kick to the defence
questions.why: Opponents must be outside the penalty area until the ball is in play.

questions.q: Can a goal be scored directly from a goal kick against the opponents?
choices: Only after it leaves the box
questions.why: A goal may be scored directly against the opponents from a goal kick.

questions.q: Can you score directly from a corner kick?
choices: Only if it is touched first
questions.why: A goal may be scored directly from a corner against the opponents.

questions.q: A corner kick is awarded when the ball crosses the goal line last touched by:
questions.why: Last touch by a defender gives a corner; last touch by an attacker gives a goal kick.

questions.q: May the corner flag be moved to make the kick easier?
choices: Yes, if it is in the way
questions.why: The corner flag must not be moved.
